proof.claim:
A mutation interrupted by a crash must end in one of exactly two states:
it never happened, or it completed exactly once.

THE FAULT. Begin a real desired-state mutation, then SIGKILL the controller
while it is in flight. Let it restart and settle.

    desired-state write begins
          ↓  SIGKILL — no shutdown, no flush, no cleanup
    controller restarts with no memory of what it was doing
          ↓
    the cluster must resolve to one of two states, and no other

THE TWO ACCEPTABLE OUTCOMES:

    the operation never happened
    the operation eventually converged exactly once

There is no third state, and in particular there is no state called "the
workflow says SUCCEEDED". This suite has already established that a child
workflow reporting SUCCEEDED is dispatch acknowledgement rather than install
proof, so "it says it worked" is not one of the permitted answers.

WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN. A desired-state record without its generation. An
artifact published twice, or once under two build_ids. A reconcile loop that
keeps retrying a half-finished transition. A release marked converged on
evidence written before the crash.

SCOPE, STATED PLAINLY. This kills at ONE boundary — the controller during a
desired-state write. The full fault matrix wants a killpoint at every durable
transition:

    publish → desired generation → dispatch → download →
    install → service start → installed receipt → converged

and running the same scenario once per boundary, with only the two outcomes
above permitted at each. That needs deterministic failpoints inside the
services, because from outside the harness cannot reliably observe the moment
between "package installed" and "receipt written" — the window is small and
unobservable, and a timing-based approximation would test whichever boundary it
happened to hit rather than the one it named. Until those failpoints exist,
this scenario covers the boundary that IS reachable and says so, rather than
claiming a matrix it does not run.

authority.note: Simulation output is evidence/candidate knowledge only. Governed promotion is required before production may rely on it.
